text: Paper · JMLR 23(120), 2022 · arXiv 2101.03961 Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity (Switch Transformer) William Fedus, Barret Zoph, Noam Shazeer Google Brain · January 2021 (arXiv v1 11 January 2021; JMLR 2022; arXiv v3 June 2022) In one line: Simplified MoE to top-1 routing with a single balancing loss and selective fp32, reaching T5-Base quality up to 7x faster at equal FLOPs per token (64-expert Switch-Base) and scaling to the 1.6T-parameter Switch-C, 4x faster than T5-XXL to a fixed perplexity and the first trillion-parameter model with reported results.

text: No-Token-Left-Behind ( Appendix B , Figure 11 ): overflowing tokens rerouted, iteratively, to their next-best expert, so almost nothing is dropped.

text: When it buys less : memory-bound deployment (distillation keeps only about 30% of the gain), reasoning-heavy fine-tuning at large scale (Appendix E), and GPU stacks with dropless kernels, which have since replaced capacity factors ( Then and now ).
label: core

text: Why it matters (beyond the paper) §9 Conclusion This is the paper that made sparse MoE practical.
label: core

text: It showed top- k with k > 1 was not necessary, compressed MoE's losses into one balancing loss, showed bfloat16 sparse training works with a local float32 router, and named the vocabulary the field still uses: expert capacity, capacity factor, token dropping, expert parallelism, sparse against active parameters.
label: core

text: It made parameter count a scaling axis separate from FLOPs, and Switch-C was the first trillion-parameter model with reported results: GShard had trained a 1T MoE in bfloat16 but "encountered several trainability issues with numerical stability, hence did not include the results" ( GShard ).
label: core

text: The lineage runs straight through GLaM (top-2 of 64 experts in every other layer, 1.2T parameters; GLaM ) and ST-MoE (router z-loss, top-2 at capacity factor 1.25; ST-MoE ) to Mixtral (top-2 of 8 coarse experts in every layer, open weights) and to DeepSeekMoE and DeepSeek-V3 (fine-grained plus shared experts, and auxiliary-loss-free bias balancing, which addresses the balance against quality tension the f · P loss introduced), and on to today's default frontier recipe of high-sparsity MoE (GPT-4-class models, Llama 4, Qwen3-MoE, Kimi K2; see Topic: llm-landscape ).
label: core

text: Its pain points were as influential as its fixes: token dropping motivated dropless kernels ( MegaBlocks : "never drops tokens"), and its instability at scale motivated the router z-loss line of work (ST-MoE).
label: core

text: Then and now: the Switch recipe, line by line Switch's recipe had eight lines: how many experts a token sees, how many experts and how big, which layers get them, how the router scores, how load is balanced, what happens when an expert is full, the router's precision, and any extra router loss.

section: then and now: the switch recipe, line by line
text: Step through six later papers and models; each cell is sourced (hover or tap the source link), a highlighted cell differs from Switch, and the counter says how many lines still read as Switch wrote them. "Not stated" means the source does not say, not that nothing changed. ◀◀ ▶ Play ▶▶ Speed 0.5× 1× 2× What survived, what changed Survived The sparse FFN as the place experts live; the router as a single linear layer whose gate value scales the expert output; an f · P balancing loss of Switch's form (as the main mechanism in Qwen3, as a small safety term in DeepSeek-V3); a router kept at higher precision than the rest; expert parallelism with all-to-all dispatch and combine.
label: core

section: then and now: the switch recipe, line by line
text: Changed One expert per token became two (GLaM, ST-MoE, Mixtral) and then eight small ones (DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3); capacity factors and dropped tokens gave way to dropless kernels (MegaBlocks, DeepSeek-V3); the balance against quality tension of the auxiliary loss led to a bias-based scheme (DeepSeek-V3) or a loss computed over the global batch (Qwen3); ST-MoE added the router z-loss for the instability Switch-XXL hit.
